David Warner Slams 'Disgraceful' Australia Batting Collapse After South Africa Test Series Defeat

31 Oct 2026, 07:01 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Sports Desk · Source: www.bbc.co.uk

2 min read

Key takeawaysFormer Australia opener David Warner delivered a scathing assessment of his former team after they collapsed to a heavy defeat against South Africa in Cape Town, securing a famous series victory for the Proteas.

Australia Crumble in Cape Town Chase

Former Australia opener David Warner delivered a scathing assessment of his former team after they collapsed to a heavy defeat against South Africa in Cape Town, securing a famous series victory for the Proteas.

Chasing a target of 288 runs to win the final Test, Australia's batting lineup unraveled dramatically on the final day. Fast bowler Kagiso Rabada struck twice in the opening over, removing openers cheaply and setting a tone of resistance that the tourists failed to match. Rabada finished with figures of 3-39, a performance that also saw him become the fastest bowler to reach 350 Test wickets.

Warner's Scathing Verdict

Speaking as a pundit on Fox Sports during the morning session, Warner did not hold back his criticism of the team's performance, labeling the display "terrible," "disgraceful," and "un-Australian."

  • Top-Order Failures: Warner highlighted a lack of fight throughout the series, noting that the batting group had repeatedly let the bowling attack down.
  • Key Dismissals: A mix of sharp bowling and self-inflicted wounds—including a mix-up resulting in Josh Inglis being run out—left Australia reeling at 60-7 by the lunch interval.
  • Spin Collapse: Spinner Simon Harmer capitalized on the pressure, claiming career-best figures of 6-16 as Australia were ultimately bowled out for just 111 runs.

Match and Series Context

South Africa's victory capped a fluctuating three-Test series, lifting the Proteas back to the top of the world rankings. For South Africa, centuries earlier in the match from Wiaan Mulder (115) and Ryan Rickelton (101) laid the foundation for their total of 387 in the second innings, building on a first-innings score of 329.

Australia's second-innings resistance was brief and unusual, featuring a 50-minute stretch where only a single run was scored as Pat Cummins and Cameron Green attempted to block their way to safety. Nathan Lyon finished as Australia's top scorer in the second innings with an unbeaten 33, while Cummins and his teammates now face mounting pressure ahead of an upcoming schedule featuring home Tests against New Zealand, a tour of India, and the Ashes.
